sn35.97:1.1: “Negligence” (_pamāda_) is from a root meaning to be mad or drunk. It’s often used in an ethical context, but here the Buddha extends it throughout the path.
sn35.97:1.5: The discourse links “negligence” with the process of mental uplifting that leads to _samādhi_ (see [sn12.23:3.11]()).
sn35.97:1.10: “Principles” (_dhammā_) such as the four noble truths, dependent origination, etc.
